questions.question_text: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is $30^{\circ}$. Find the size of each interior angle.

options.why: Subtracted $30$ from $360$ instead of $180$.
Subtracted $30$ from $90$, treating the angles as complementary.
Found the number of sides $360\div30$ instead of the interior angle.

questions.solution_text:
Interior and exterior angles are supplementary.
$I=180^{\circ}-30^{\circ}$
$=150^{\circ}$

options.text: No, because $360\div16=22.5$ is not a whole number

options.why: Rounded $22.5$ down to a whole number of sides.
Read the exterior angle as the number of sides.
